name: Processor D
justification: Benchmarking on Processor A revealed severe routing bottlenecks: while simplified 1D linear nearest-neighbor HEA artificially avoids SWAPs, the complete molecular orbital interaction graph of H2 STO-3G requires all-to-all cross-orbital entanglement across spin-orbitals {0,1,2,3}. On Processor A's acyclic tree topology, executing this complete K4 molecular interaction graph forces 2 SWAPs (+6 CX gates, +100% two-qubit overhead), doubling two-qubit depth from 5 to 12. Processor B avoids SWAPs but suffers from degree-5 hub crowding on node 6 (violating degree <= 4) and a diameter of 4. Processor D resolves these bottlenecks through a 6-qubit chordal ring featuring an all-to-all K4 chemistry core on qubits {0,1,2,3} with cross-chords (0,2) and (1,3), executing the full molecular interaction graph with 0 SWAPs (cx_overhead = 0) while strictly obeying max degree <= 4. Error rates match official standards (0.001/0.005/0.01) to isolate topological routing gains. In exchange, Processor D accepts a degree of 4 on bridge nodes 2 and 3, increasing planar control line density and microwave crosstalk.
